doc.title: Mr. and Mrs. A.C. Synigal and B. Bozant Interview, 1962-05-17
doc.interviewee: Mr. and Mrs. A.C. Synigal and B. Bozant

title: Preference for Dixieland over rock and roll
summary: The women say they love Dixieland jazz and that young people enjoy it despite rock and roll.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: You know, recently they said about the old musicians, they didn't have very many left. But you would be surprised how many they do have left that no one. I know quite a few right around here. Oh yeah. And I bet there's a lot still that you don't know that has valuable information. Oh yeah. Oh yeah. That's right. They're living. They're very old, but they're here. What kind of music do you prefer? Well, I do love jazz music. Well, it's everything in its place, but I do love Dixieland jazz in preference to progressive, or even rock and roll. I do love it. I'm not saying that because you were interviewing us, but it's a thing I always liked from a child. And of course, my aunt, living with us all these years, she played only that type of music. So naturally, I guess it just stayed imprinted in us. And it's what I really love. And you, Mrs. Senegal? I prefer jazz music. I hope it never dies out. Yeah. They sing. I prefer Stixieland music. I see some youngsters never working on a lot.
Because if you're not even dancing, it peps to you.

You know, the youngsters claim that they are going head over here for rock and roll. But some of our members bring their children and their grandchildren and give them invitations to our ball. And I noticed they enjoy themselves mighty well with that Dixieland music. Oh, more than their own dances. And they come every year. Yes, indeed. So they enjoy it, but I guess because rock and roll has taken over so much, they think they like it best. But actually, I think deep down in them, they like them for Dixieland. Yes. It's just in them. They will come around where a band's playing, or you'll see them in the second line. There'll be kids following a parade band or something, and they're certainly enjoying it, whether they'll admit it or not. Which proves that Dixieland is best. I mean, if they didn't enjoy it, they wouldn't bother to come around.
